items.note: Full yellow band with a sagging arc, a 64px-class bold tight headline, a blue pill plus a white on-field pill, then a confetti 'Browse the docs' heading, cream cards with category-hue pictogram covers and a navy chat vignette. Clearly the reference's language, as in 01/02/06. The hero art is a hexagon, disc and cloud stamp about a fifth of the band wide. It pictures nothing about the product, where the reference's 02 scene balances the headline.

Centered yellow hero with a bold two-line headline, stacked blue and white pills and a sag arc, close to the reference phone (04). The shape stamp is stacked as its own row under the pills, so the band fills the whole first screen and no content shows.

Navy page and indigo sidebar under the same yellow hero band, with navy cards and a violet vignette panel. A convincing night palette in the spirit of 03. It shares the light screen's small, meaningless hero stamp.

The navy header has an indigo menu pill and search, over the yellow centered hero, and it reads as the reference's night language. Further down, the page ends in a bright white bottom bar under the indigo footer, which breaks the night palette that 03 keeps dark to the edge.

Compact blue header band with breadcrumb, bold title and a sag arc, an ink selected nav pill with a white dot, cream TOC and code panels, ink and cream package-manager pills, and cream callouts. Well-ordered and recognisably the system. The header art is a disc-and-pill sticker that pictures nothing about installing.

Blue header band with a large bold title, a cream TOC panel and generous reading type, faithful to the reference's mobile rhythm. The breadcrumb wraps beside the corner cluster and leaves a lone '/ Installation' on its own line.

Same structure at night: blue band on navy, indigo TOC, a white selected nav pill with a dark dot. A clean, consistent dark rendering. It has the same small disc-and-pill header stamp as the light screen.
Blue band on navy with an indigo TOC panel and a readable body column, matching its light twin. The wrapped breadcrumb with an orphaned separator beside the cluster repeats here.

Green area band (the Guides hue, consistent with the sidebar dots), a cream code panel with a Copy pill, plain reference tables and cream callouts. Area-hue mapping is handled as the reference would. The header art is again a two-piece pill-and-disc sticker.

Green band, cream TOC and long-form body read calmly and on-system. At the page foot, the prev/next and helpful cards carry a ring, a zigzag and blob glyphs unrelated to their labels. The reference (05) chooses each glyph to mean its row.
Green band over navy, indigo code and TOC panels, and a white selected nav pill. A faithful night version of a dense reference page, with the same sticker-sized header art.
Indigo tables, code and callouts on navy stay legible, and wide tables scroll inside their panels. The page still ends in the white bottom bar under the indigo footer.

Pink area band (the Changelog top-nav dot matches it) with a cloud-and-sun cluster, cream release cards with dot tags and a cream TOC. Tone-on-tone depth as in 06/09. The cluster is a small corner stamp rather than a scene.

Pink band with a sag arc, then cream TOC and release cards in a readable column, close to the reference's mobile stacking. The change tags differ in width, so the entry text starts at a different indent on each line instead of aligning in one column.
The pink band stays full-strength over navy, with indigo release cards and TOC. A coherent night page with the same small corner cluster as the light screen.
Indigo release cards on navy read well, but the page closes on a bright white bottom bar under the indigo footer, the one light element at night.

findings.summary: This finding from rc.3 reviews 1 and 2 still holds on the holdout app. Every desktop band's art is a compact two-to-three-piece stamp about 200–300px wide, roughly a fifth of the band: a hexagon, disc and cloud on the front page; a disc and pill, a pill and disc, or a cloud and sun on the inner pages. None of them pictures the page's subject, and a wide empty stretch of colour sits between the text and the art. The reference's hero (02) is a layered scene about as wide as the text, and it balances the headline.
findings.promptFix: Size header-band art by width: the art box is about 40–45% of the band, and the SVG is width 100% and height auto in a wide viewBox. Build it from 4–5 pieces: a lead shape that pictures the screen's subject in one noun, a second-hue shape cutting into it, a 48–64px four-point star, a small sparkle and optionally a cloud. Give several sample clusters with different silhouettes, labelled as structure only. Art narrower than a third of the band, or a disc and pill that picture nothing, is a sticker, not a scene.
findings.specRule: .ms-field__art > svg { height: 100%; min-height: var(--size-art); max-width: 100%; } … <!-- Header-band cluster, one of many: lead hexagon, overlapping pill, large star + small sparkle --> <svg viewBox="0 0 240 200">

findings.summary: In dark mode, every page ends in a bright white bottom bar under the indigo footer. This is the same spec-caused break of the night palette named in rc.3 review-2, and it is still open. The reference's night band (03) stays dark to the edge.
findings.promptFix: The footer bottom bar is the darkest surface in both appearances: ink by day, and at night a step darker than the navy page, set through a dedicated role token. Keep `surface.inverse` for small floating pieces such as toasts, never for a full-width bar.
findings.specRule: Footer | Cream band with rise arc, link columns, a signup field + ink pill; `surface.inverse` bottom bar with round icon buttons … (dark) `color.surface.inverse` | `#ffffff`

findings.summary: On phones, the front-page hero stacks its art as a separate row under the pills, so the yellow band fills the entire first screen and no content shows. The reference phone (04) keeps the hero compact, with art tucked at the edge.

The page-foot navigation and feedback cards each carry a decorative glyph (a ring, a zigzag, blobs) that has nothing to do with the card's label. The reference (05) chooses each row's glyph to picture its topic.
On phones, the header band's breadcrumb is squeezed beside the corner cluster and wraps, leaving a separator and the current page alone on a second line.

Change-type tags in the release entries size to their label, so the entry text after them starts at a different indent on each line. The column looks ragged where the reference keeps list text on one clean edge.
